sections.text:
Zechariah encouraged the same returned community as Haggai. The first part of the book (chapters 1 to 8) contains eight night visions and messages that promise God’s return to Jerusalem and call for justice and mercy.

The second part (9 to 14) is harder to place. It speaks of a humble king riding on a donkey, of a shepherd who is struck, of one who is pierced and mourned, and of a day when the LORD will be king over all the earth.
The dated messages fall between 520 and 518 before Christ. Many scholars think chapters 9 to 14 come from a later time; others hold that Zechariah wrote the whole book.

The Gospels quote Zechariah repeatedly in telling of Jesus’ last week: the entry into Jerusalem on a donkey, the thirty pieces of silver, the scattered sheep and the pierced one. Christians differ on how much of the final chapters still lies ahead.
